name: Participating Forward
summary: An unbalanced risk reversal - long 2 calls against 1 short put - giving full upside participation on part of the notional while taking downside exposure on a smaller amount; the core FX corporate-hedging structure rendered in share-settled options.

legs.strike_rule: ATM or slightly OTM, call delta 0.45-0.55
|put delta| 0.30-0.45, struck so the put's premium pays for both calls (net cost <= 0)

max_profit: UNLIMITED - 2 x $100 per point above the call strike
max_loss: (put strike x 100) - net credit, if the underlying goes to zero; downside participation is half the upside
breakevens: upside = call strike + net debit per share / 2; downside = put strike - net credit per share
when_to_use: When the system wants leveraged upside on an ETF it is willing to own at the put strike, financed by that willingness - a hedging-desk structure repurposed as a stock-replacement with a built-in entry order.
entry_rules: Underlying must be an ETF or mega-cap the account is genuinely willing to own 100 shares of at the put strike.

LEVEL 3 CONSTRAINT: the short put must be cash-secured - hold put strike x 100 in cash. On a $50k account that caps the underlying at roughly $150-$200 per share alongside other positions. If cash is unavailable, convert the short put into a put credit spread and accept the smaller credit.
Ratio fixed at 2 long calls : 1 short put. Never invert it (1 call vs 2 puts) - that is a naked ratio.
Net cost <= 0 (a true participating forward is zero-cost) and IV rank <= 40 so the long calls are not overpaid.
Both legs same expiry, OI >= 250, single MLeg order.
No earnings inside the option's life for single names.
management_rules: Take profit when the long calls reach 100% gain, or roll them up and out and leave the short put to decay.
Buy back the short put at 50% of its premium - the financing job is done.
If |put delta| reaches 0.60, either close the put or prepare cash to accept the shares; never roll it down and out more than once.
Time stop at 21 DTE on the short put regardless of the calls.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: flatten the short put by 15:30 ET on expiration day, always.
Close the short put at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85 - early assignment on an American put is a real risk once it is deep ITM.
Close the long calls rather than exercising; exercise would buy 200 shares.
If the short put is closed for a loss, re-evaluate the calls as a standalone long - do not keep the ratio alive by selling another put.
assignment_risk: One assignable short put, cash-secured. Assignment delivers 100 shares at the strike while the 2 long calls remain - survivable, but it consumes the account's cash and is exactly what the guards exist to prevent.
buying_power: put strike x 100 in cash (or spread width x 100 if converted), plus the calls' net debit.
liquidity_needs: Liquid chain at both strikes; the 2:1 ratio must be fillable as one ticket or legged in the order put-first.
common_mistakes: Choosing the put strike purely to reach zero cost and ending up with a put the account cannot actually afford to be assigned on; treating the 2x calls as 2x the risk when the risk is all in the single put.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - the structure is a multi-month participation trade.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
